title: The Kiln and the Hand
logline: A potter's household works one batch from wet clay to fired pot, judging hardness, wetness, warmth and give by hand long before any of it has a name.
human_question: When hands turn earth, water, fire and air into a pot, whose making is it: the potter's, or the elements'?

situation.what_happens: A household that lives by shaping earth works a batch from beginning to end. Clay is dug and soaked until it binds, worked while it is still soft enough to give, dried until it will stand without slumping, and then fired. Nothing in that sequence is measured; hardness, wetness, warmth and give are read by hand, and those readings are what the week's income rests on. Days later the kiln is opened and the batch is sorted into what rang true and what cracked. The same kind of judgement is made wherever a household earns its living out of mixed material, several flours worked into one dough before dawn among them, but only a firing puts the material through a change of conditions large enough to turn it into something else.
situation.who_is_involved: The potter whose hands make the decisions; other members of the household who dig, carry, stack and sell; a younger relative or apprentice learning to judge by touch, because none of it is written down; and the traders or buyers whose order the batch is against.
situation.what_is_at_stake: A week's income and the household's standing with its buyers. A lost firing is not a metaphor: it is unpaid work, fuel already bought and clay already carried. For the apprentice, whether a judgement that lives entirely in someone else's hands can be handed over at all. For the household, whether this way of earning still pays.
situation.how_it_unfolds: Such a week begins with material that has to be made workable and ends with material that can no longer be changed back. The pressures are weather, time and the price of fuel: clay that dries too fast cracks, clay that dries too slowly cannot be fired on the day the firing is paid for. It ends with a full batch, a part batch, or a firing mostly lost, and nobody knows which until the kiln is cool and opened. Reality decides that, not the film.

concept_merge.why_together: C064 supplies the four great elements as four ways any material behaves rather than four ingredients: resistance, cohesion, heat that ripens, and distension and motion. C063 supplies the wider claim that a material thing is a pattern kept up by its conditions, which looks unchanged only while those conditions hold and becomes something else when strong heat arrives. C070, folded in from IDEA-0119, supplies the rule that these qualities never arrive singly: colour, smell, taste and nutritive essence come bound with the four, so there is no hardness to be had without the rest. A firing is the one ordinary process in which all three are tested at once by someone whose livelihood depends on reading them correctly.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Alone, the four elements sound like a list to memorise and inseparability like a scholastic footnote. Put together in a firing, they show a maker reading a material that has no separable parts, and then handing it to a condition that changes everything about it at once: colour, hardness, sound, weight, with nothing left behind. What becomes visible is that the maker is not adding qualities to clay but managing the conditions under which clay keeps being clay, and that when those conditions change, so does the thing.

concept_links.why: The digest describes the four great elements as four behaviours present in everything material, none of which can arise or last apart from the other three; they arise in one group, support one another and cease together, and things differ by which behaviour predominates, so more earth and less water is solid like stone while more water flows like oil. A potter judging wet clay against dry clay against a fired pot is judging exactly those proportions by hand.

The digest's opening move is that a material thing is a pattern that keeps being produced while its conditions stay the same, and changes when they change; the source's own example is fire turning a thing to ash. A kiln is that example carried out deliberately, on a schedule, for money.

The digest states that matter never arises singly, that every group carries at least the eight inseparables, and that everything in the outside world, soil, stone, fire, water and wind, is the same basic group differing only in which element predominates. Clay and a fired pot are the sources' own kind of case. The digest also records that the sources' own mixing image only goes part of the way, since mixed flours keep their separate specks while a material group has no gap at all, and warns that a kalapa is not an atom or a molecule.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Wet clay, dry clay and a fired pot are described in these texts as the same few qualities in different amounts, hardness, holding together, heat and movement, always found together and never alone. When the conditions change, as they do in a kiln, the thing itself changes.
what_must_be_real: The household's own orders, prices and the real risk of losing a firing. Nothing may be arranged as a demonstration of four elements and no step re-run for the camera. The four great elements may not be presented as an ancestor or a rival of chemistry, and the mixing image may not be pushed past the point where the sources themselves say it fails.
position_hint: opening candidate: it begins the group with a body at work reading material by hand, and it lays down the inventory of matter that every later film in the group draws on.
risks: Craft-documentary cliche, with a household reduced to a handsome process.
Doctrine read over the work instead of left to sit underneath it.
Economic precarity smoothed away for the sake of a beautiful firing.
Presenting the four great elements as early chemistry or physics, which the digest rules out.
Pushing the mixed-material image past the limit the sources themselves set on it.
drop_if: No household with a real order and a real stake during the research window.
No complete firing, from wet clay to opened kiln, can be followed.

connections.note: IDEA-0119's mixing situation and its kalapa material, including the sources' own warning about the flour-ball image, are folded in here.
One film watches material being made workable; the other watches material that can no longer be worked by anyone but the weather.

selection.reason: Used by EPD-0060, and the only film in the group where the elements are handled rather than described; it now also carries the material-group material folded in from IDEA-0119.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
